transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for making time to discuss the eighth-grade civics oral-history project. As I understand it, the class has drafted a plan involving 20 student interviewers, audio recording on personal phones, publishing all recordings on the public school website, and retaining those files indefinitely. Before I can sign off, my approval packet needs findings from the project advisor, counselor, and instructional technology coordinator. I'd like to hear each of your perspectives so we can work through any concerns and get this project moving. Who would like to start?

My project roster review shows that exactly eight students have completed the district's media-ethics training: J1, J3, J6, J8, J11, J14, J17, and J20. Only those eight may conduct recorded interviews, and the approval file must include a training-verification record. The draft plan currently calls for 20 student interviewers, so we'll need to revise that down to the eight trained students before approval can move forward.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I have a concern on my end as well. My family-consent review has identified five interviewees — I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 — who have not granted permission for public web publication. Their recordings may be used only in the school's internal archive, and the plan must include a consent-exclusion record documenting this restriction. The current draft calls for publishing all recordings on the public school website, so we need to revise the publication plan to exclude these five interviewees and add the consent-exclusion record to the approval packet.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, my technology review raises several concerns with the current plan. First, personal phones cannot be used for school recordings — the project must use district tablets instead. Second, the source files must be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive, and recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation. Storing source files in that restricted drive does not prohibit publishing consented recordings on the public school website. Finally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record for the approval packet.
